caveat: Predicts which PAIR a human clicked. Not evidence that the pair wins more games.

STATUS.state: NOT RETIRED — stale (46 features vs board.js 48) and NEVER WIRED IN. Refit and wire, do not discard.
STATUS.retirement_reversed_because: Will: teams must optimise for TEAM success, not individual Pokemon success, and a bot that decides each slot independently is systematically exploitable. He is right and the earlier retirement was reasoned from the wrong evidence.
STATUS.what_was_wrong_with_retiring_it: It was retired on the double-target rate (MAG 24.6% vs humans 23.2%). That metric touches 2 of the 18 joint features — bothSameTarget and overkill. The other 16 are coordination the rate cannot see: focusFireKills, redirectThenAttack, boostsPartnerDamage, speedSetupHelpsPartner, weatherSetupHelpsPartner, healsPartner, doubleKO, flinchThenSetup, screenWhileThreatened, spreadFreeBesideAlly and the rest. Judging a coordination model by a targeting statistic is judging a ninth of it.
STATUS.the_real_argument: It has NEVER been wired into magnemite.js, so the project has never tested whether coordinated choice helps. Retiring it would have closed a question that was never opened.
STATUS.exploitability: A policy that picks each slot independently can be set positions that REQUIRE coordination and will fail them every time. That is a repeatable hole, not variance — exactly what engine/exploit.js (WOBBUFFET) searches for.
